definitions.explanation: A shop specializing in selling fresh fish and seafood, or the person who runs such a shop.

examples.japanese: {魚屋|さかなや}で{刺身|さしみ}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought sashimi at the fish shop.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}の{魚屋|さかなや}はいつも{新鮮|しんせん}な{魚|さかな}を{置|お}いている。
examples.english: The fish shop in front of the station always has fresh fish.

examples.japanese: {商店街|しょうてんがい}の{魚屋|さかなや}は{三代|さんだい}{続|つづ}く{老舗|しにせ}だ。
examples.english: The fish shop on the shopping street is a long-established store that has been in business for three generations.

notes:
Compound of {魚|さかな} (fish) + {屋|や} (shop/dealer).

The suffix ～{屋|や} is used for many types of specialty shops and their proprietors:
- {肉屋|にくや} (butcher shop)
- {八百屋|やおや} (greengrocer)
- {花屋|はなや} (florist)
- {本屋|ほんや} (bookshop)

Traditional {魚屋|さかなや} are often found in {商店街|しょうてんがい} (shopping arcades) and at {市場|いちば} (markets). While supermarkets have replaced many independent fish shops, dedicated {魚屋|さかなや} remain valued for their expertise in selecting and preparing fish.
